data.reasoning: Both models independently analyzed the same 4 files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, config.x86_64, LICENSE) and found no security issues. The package is a standard Linux kernel build with pinned sources from kernel.org, proper checksums, PGP verification, and normal build/package functions. The only disagreement was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400) on the LICENSE file in Report 1, not by any security finding. License files contain no executable code and pose no injection risk.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was purely mechanical: qwen3-235b failed to audit the LICENSE file due to an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in an inconclusive verdict. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed the same file and found it to be a standard ISC license with no security concerns. Both models' actual security analysis of the PKGBUILD and other files was consistent and correct.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) experienced a tool error on LICENSE file (HTTP 400), but this is non-critical as license files contain no executable code
learnings: Tool errors on non-executable files (LICENSE, README, etc.) should not force an inconclusive verdict when all executable files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches) have been successfully audited and found safe

The audit tool should distinguish between 'file failed to audit' and 'file contains security issues' - a missing audit of a benign file type should not override positive security findings from critical files
Consider implementing a fallback or retry mechanism for transient API errors to prevent tool failures from affecting final verdicts
